description: In PHP_FUNCTION(imageloadfont) at ext/gd/gd.c:543, the loop that reads the font header passes `&font[b]` as the destination buffer, where `font` is a typed gdFontPtr rather than a char*. Pointer arithmetic therefore scales the offset by sizeof(gdFont) (~24 bytes) instead of 1. If the first php_stream_read() returns fewer than hdr_size bytes, `b` is set to that byte count and the next iteration writes to `(char*)font + b*24`, well beyond the single-struct allocation. An attacker who can influence the font stream — via an uploaded file, a URL wrapper, or any transport that produces a short read — controls the bytes written at this predictable out-of-bounds heap offset, corrupting adjacent zend_mm metadata or live objects and enabling a heap-grooming path to code execution.
reproduction: 1. Identify an endpoint that passes user-controlled data to imageloadfont() (e.g., theme/font upload or remote font URL).
2. Serve or upload a font stream engineered so the initial php_stream_read() returns n < hdr_size bytes.
3. On the next loop iteration, PHP writes attacker-chosen bytes to `(char*)font + n*sizeof(gdFont)`.
4. Groom the heap so the OOB write lands on zend_mm chunk metadata or a live object.
5. Leverage the corrupted metadata/object to achieve arbitrary code execution.
technical_details: The root cause is incorrect pointer arithmetic: `&font[b]` indexes a gdFontPtr, so each unit of `b` advances sizeof(gdFont) bytes rather than one byte. After a partial read of n bytes, the resumed read targets `(char*)font + n*sizeof(gdFont)` instead of `(char*)font + n`, landing outside the ~24-byte header buffer and writing attacker-supplied data onto neighboring heap memory.
title: Heap out-of-bounds write in font loader via stride miscalculation
